scope.summary: Introduce the first oya-ci-gate-contract remediation POC crate with a pure remediate() contract, per-code remediation tiers, and an idempotence regression proving the described edit returns None after the same face is fixed.
explicit_non_claims: No write-capable remediation applier is introduced; remediate() returns described data only.
No generated faces, .github workflow, release-governance, or unrelated SDK/runtime files are changed.
Only one fixture gate/code is used as the REMED-001 proof of concept; rollout to additional gates is deferred to later serialized cards.

facets.F1_correctness: The Gate trait exposes pure evaluate_keyed and remediate siblings, and the fixture gate declares manifest_missing_license as AutoFix while returning Remediation::None on the fixed face.
facets.F2_tests: Cargo and Buck2 unit tests cover bare-code projection, described edit output, idempotent None after fix, block-rationale validation, duplicate-code rejection, and byte-range validation.
facets.F3_maintainability: The contract surface is isolated in libs/oya-ci-gate-contract with a narrow public API, serde data types, and no side-effecting remediation delivery logic.
facets.F4_compatibility: Workspace inclusion uses the existing libs/oya-* glob; Cargo.lock contains only the new workspace package entry and serde dependencies, and capability-membership maps the new gate-contract crate to the existing build/CI meta home.
facets.F5_security: The crate forbids unsafe code and keeps write authority outside gate implementations; AutoFix remains described data rather than an applied mutation.
facets.F6_privacy: The contract carries no tenant, customer, or personal data and only models generic gate findings/remediation descriptions.
facets.F7_operability: The Buck2 target and unittest make the contract consumable by cloud-ci gate jobs as well as local Cargo workflows.
facets.F8_performance: The implementation is simple in-memory data projection using BTreeSet for deterministic reports; no runtime service path is introduced.
facets.F9_compliance: ADR-0528 and ADR-0529 safety boundaries are preserved: remediation is pure, per-code tiers are explicit, semantic changes use Block rationale, and idempotence is tested.
facets.F10_reversibility: The PR adds one isolated crate and lockfile entry; reverting the PR removes the contract POC without data migration or deployed state changes.
facets.F11_observability: The evidence packet records task, branch, files, verification, review evidence, and remaining GitHub protected-context governance.
facets.F13_migration: Only the first remediation contract POC is introduced; migrating existing gates to this contract is explicitly deferred to future serialized remediation/gate cards.
facets.A1_naming_adherence: The crate name oya-ci-gate-contract matches ADR-0528 and the existing workspace oya-* naming contract.
facets.A2_documentation_adherence: Rust module docs cite ADR-0515 and ADR-0528 and explain that described edits are delivered by privileged callers outside this contract.
facets.A3_structure_adherence: Cargo.toml, BUCK, and src/lib.rs follow neighboring first-party Rust crate conventions.
facets.A4_architecture_adherence: The change keeps detection/remediation at the gate-contract boundary and leaves applied-edit delivery to the ADR-0531-style privileged layer.
facets.A5_dependency_adherence: Only existing workspace dependencies serde and serde_json are used; no new third-party dependency is introduced, and the new crate is explicitly mapped in specs/capability-registry.json rather than expanding the frozen unmapped baseline.
facets.A6_schema_adherence: Serde rename conventions make Verdict, Remediation, and RemediationTier stable machine-readable wire/data shapes.
facets.A7_algorithm_adherence: The fixture remediation checks the same face predicate as evaluate_keyed so rerunning after the fix is present returns None.

review_evidence.note: Prior independent review approved the REMED-001 scope; this PR binds the same approved diff to a clean current origin/dev branch and protected CI governance.

verification_evidence: cargo test -p oya-cloud-ci-capability-membership-app live_crate_corpus_is_born_advisory_green --test capability_membership: PASS after mapping libs/oya-ci-gate-contract to build/
known_gaps: GitHub oya-ci-required and branch-protection review remain PR governance gates after push/open.
Additional real gate integrations and applied-edit delivery are intentionally outside REMED-001.
